title: still fails the same rule on an element that is not a sample card
why: An excuse that no longer asks the element for its selector excuses the rule everywhere, so a new instance elsewhere passes.

title: still fails another rule on a sample card
why: An excuse that ignores its rule lets any new rule through on the cards.

title: fails an entry that matched nothing on a sweep it is expected on
why: With staleness unchecked, the list outlives the defect it was written for.

title: does not ask for an entry on a sweep it is not expected on
why: Asking every sweep for the entry fails the screens that have no cards.

title: lists incomplete results and never drops them
why: Dropping incomplete results makes what axe could not decide read as a pass.

title: gives nothing when the selector names several elements
why: Answering for the first of several elements excuses a node on the strength of a different element.

title: gives nothing for an element that is not a sample card
why: Not asking the element lets every node match every excuse.

title: judges an entry in its themes alone, for excuses and for staleness
why: An entry that ignores its themes excuses Night's contrast in Parchment too, and is called stale where it was never due.
